targetAudience: PMs and engineers building multi-step agents
topic: Your agent demo succeeded 9 times. Why it still fails in production
coreInsight: Per-step reliability multiplies across long tasks, so evaluate end-to-end task success over many runs instead of trusting a few successful demos.

hookVariants.text: Agents don’t fail at a step. They fail at the sum.
The math that breaks long agent tasks.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): concrete, intriguing, and the reel backs it with a labelled illustrative calculation.

script.onScreen: THE DEMO / Every step worked. / STEP 1 Read the request · STEP 2 Find the record · STEP 3 Update the system · STEP 4 Send the reply
script.voiceover: In the demo, every step worked: read the request, find the record, update the system, send the reply.

script.onScreen: WHY IT BREAKS [ILLUSTRATIVE] / ONE STEP 95% / 10 STEPS IN A ROW 60% / Errors compound.
script.voiceover: Illustrative math: if each step succeeds ninety-five percent of the time, ten steps in a row succeed about sixty percent of the time. Errors compound.

script.onScreen: Test the whole task, not one step. / Share this with your agent team
script.voiceover: Test the whole task, not one step. Share this with your agent team.

caption:
A step that works 95% of the time sounds solid. Chain ten of them and it’s closer to a coin flip with good odds.

Illustrative math (assuming independent steps): 0.95 × 0.95 … ten times ≈ 0.60. Real systems differ, but the direction holds: long tasks amplify small error rates.

So evaluate the whole task, many times:
→ end-to-end success rate over dozens of runs
→ where in the chain failures cluster
→ which steps need a check or a human approval

(Numbers in the reel are illustrative, not measurements of a real system.)
